# PhysicsHand

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Runtime/Scripts/Interaction/PhysicsHand.cs#L23)

The middle layer of the three-layer hand: a real rigidbody that chases the tracked hand with
clamped force instead of being teleported onto it. Because it is solved rather than placed, it
stops at walls, presses on what it touches, feels the weight of what it holds, and carries a
believable velocity into a throw.

The tracked hand above it is the raw XR Hands pose and never collides. The visual hand below
it follows this body, not the tracked pose, so what the player sees is what the physics
actually did.

Tracking is sampled and the body is stepped through [`SampleTracking(float)`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/PhysicsHand#sampletracking-single) and
[`Step(float, float)`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/PhysicsHand#step-single-single), which are given the current time rather than reading it. In play mode
the Unity messages pass the engine clock; anything driving the hand itself passes its own,
which is what lets it run under `Physics.Simulate`with no play mode and no device.

```csharp
[RequireComponent(typeof(Rigidbody))]
public class PhysicsHand : MonoBehaviour
```

## Methods

### Brace(Vector3, float) {#brace-vector3-single}

Tells the hand its fingers are resting on something, so it will not drive itself into it.

Taken out of the hand's own push rather than answered with a push of its own. Removing a
push only ever takes away, so it cannot add energy in any direction; an opposing force
would be added to whatever else is acting on the hand and would shove it back off a
surface the palm was already resting on.

Lasts one step and has to be set again, so leaving a surface needs no announcement.

```csharp
public void Brace(Vector3 normal, float capacity)
```

### CommandedGrip(float) {#commandedgrip-single}

Where the tracked hand is asking this grip to be at the end of the step. The raw command, before
the physics hand has had any say in it.

What a written hold aims at, and it has to be the tracked pose rather than the hand's own:
while holding, the hand follows the object, so deriving the object's target from the hand
as well would be a loop with nothing driving it.

So the hand's strength does not reach the object through this path. The world still stops
a held object through its own colliders; a hand blocked while its object is free is left
behind, which is what break distance is for.

```csharp
public Pose CommandedGrip(float stepEndTime)
```

| --- | --- | --- |

### CommandedPose(float) {#commandedpose-single}

Where the tracked hand is asking the hand itself to be at the end of this step, before the grip
offset is applied.

Wanted separately from [`CommandedGrip(float)`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/PhysicsHand#commandedgrip-single) wherever the answer should not depend
on how the hand is turned: the grip sits out from the palm, so a wrist turning on the spot
swings it through an arc while the hand itself has gone nowhere.

### Displace(Pose) {#displace-pose}

Moves a pose out of the tracked hand's frame and into this hand's, as one rigid displacement
about the tracked pose.

How anything drawn from the tracking gets drawn where the hand actually ended up. The
tracked hand is where the player's real hand is; this body is where their hand in the
world managed to get to, which differs once a wall or a held object is in the way.

A displacement rather than an assignment, so a whole skeleton can be passed through it
joint by joint and keep its shape: only where the hand is changes, never how it is posed.

```csharp
public Pose Displace(Pose tracked)
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tracked` | [`Pose`](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Pose.html) | A pose in the tracked hand's frame. |

**Returns** [`Pose`](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Pose.html)
